question: I'm a BA junior (P-025) with dual Finance and BAT concentrations and an Economics minor. Is graduating in Spring 2027 (my expected graduation) feasible given my current progress and the courses offered?

domain_contributions.programs: P-025 has 37 courses completed; dual concentration + Econ minor creates significant remaining requirement load; identifying what's left is critical
domain_contributions.schedules: Finance/BAT/Econ courses offered Spring 2026 (and will need Fall 2026 as well): 70-401, 70-416, 70-441, 70-460, 73-421, etc.
domain_contributions.policies: P-025 in good standing; may need advisor-approved overloads in some semesters; dual concentration creates scheduling risk

key_facts: P-025 has 37 courses at junior level — approximately 2 more years of coursework expected
Spring 2027 target = 3 more semesters (Spring 2026, Fall 2026, Spring 2027)
Dual concentration + minor creates heavy requirement overlap and scheduling complexity
Some Finance/BAT electives may only be offered once per year — Spring 2026 availability determines Fall 2026 planning
If overloads are needed to fit everything in 3 semesters, advisor approval required
Feasibility is plausible but tight — requires careful semester-by-semester planning
wrong_if_single_domain: Knowing program requirements reveals the heavy remaining load but not whether courses are available each semester. Knowing only the schedule cannot determine what P-025 still needs. Policy context about overloads determines whether tight semesters are feasible.
common_mistake: Treating each concentration and the minor independently without checking for semester availability bottlenecks; not accounting for courses only offered in specific semesters
reasoning_chain: Step 1 (programs): Audit remaining Finance + BAT + Econ minor requirements for P-025
Step 2 (schedules): Identify which are available Spring 2026 vs Fall 2026 vs Spring 2027
Step 3 (policies): Some semesters may require overload — advisor approval needed
Conclusion: Spring 2027 graduation is feasible but requires careful 3-semester plan with possible overloads
